title: Count the bottleneck
goal:
Figure 5 compares a two-layer block for ResNet-34 with a three-layer "bottleneck" block for ResNet-50/101/152 on 56×56 feature maps (Section 4.1). The two designs have similar time complexity. The paper also says that replacing the identity shortcut of a bottleneck with a projection doubles its size, "as the shortcut is connected to the two high-dimensional ends."

Count the weights. Skip biases and batch normalization. Write `conv_params(k, c_in, c_out)`, `basic_block_params(c)`, `bottleneck_params(c_out, c_mid)`, and `projection_shortcut_extra_params(c_out)`. The projection is a 1×1 convolution from `c_out` to `c_out` channels.
hints: A $k \times k$ convolution from $c_{\text{in}}$ to $c_{\text{out}}$ channels has $k^2 \, c_{\text{in}} \, c_{\text{out}}$ weights. The kernel size enters squared.
The bottleneck has three convolutions: 1×1 from `c_out` to `c_mid`, 3×3 from `c_mid` to `c_mid`, and 1×1 from `c_mid` back to `c_out`.
The basic block is two 3×3 convolutions with the same width at both ends, so call `conv_params(3, c, c)` twice.
